title: DataAccessV1dot3
description: K-05 v1.3, a minor version of the data-access calls (T-1137, from T-315's round 1 NEED, items 4 to 6; DL-319). It only adds to v1.2 (data-access.v1.2.schema.json, frozen and unchanged, referred to here, which refers on to v1.1 and v1): every v1.2 definition is here under its own name, by reference, and none changes, so every v1, v1.1 and v1.2 exchange is a v1.3 exchange. Added: three reads on PostgreSQL's primary, uncached (arch 02 line 117; arch 10 lines 504, 538), each stating its role and business scope (arch 10 line 546; K-04 v1 rule 4; STATE notes 5 and 22), shaped to the action-layer port it serves: readOpenHolds (the commit's OpenHolds: the open K-34 safety holds on the turn's handle and the texts with no safety row yet; closes v1.2 open gap 26), readOutboxRow (compose input's ComposeRow and finalize's FinalizeRow: an outbox row with its turn, bundle, step and line, reader, slot source and the texts it answers, never their words) and readFixedLineFacts (the fixed-line inserter's FixedLineFacts: whether Rosie texted the handle about the row's business before, and when the opt-out line was first delivered to its phone). Not model-facing, so number and length limits are schema rules here. Owner: the architect.

releaseRule.title: ReleaseRule
releaseRule.description: When a safety hold's routine actions are released (K-34 v1 safety_holds.release_rule; arch 06 lines 317 to 327): at_once (after the outcome's message: No, Safety steps then go on, Harm to a child or older adult, Needs the business's own line), when_private (once the booking is made private: Unsafe at home), after_safe (after a clear 'we're safe' with a fresh read-back: An emergency, Crisis words, Unsure), never (A threat to staff or others). The same words K-09 v1 safetyHold.releaseRule carries, which the commit's hold rules read (actions/src/commit/hold.ts letsThrough). New in v1.3.

openHold.title: OpenHold
openHold.description: One open safety hold on the turn's handle (K-34 v1 safety_holds with released_at null: safety_holds_open_handle_idx, 'The gate checks a handle's open holds before any routine commit'), with what it holds back: its release rule, which says which parts it lets through (arch 06 lines 317 to 329; CQ-65 with DL-127 and DL-128), whether the plug-in's stop words block booking (A3-26), and the booking the held actions are about. holdId, releaseRule and blocksBooking are K-09 v1 safetyHold's three fields under the same names and values (tool-api.v1.schema.json recordSafetyOutcome.response.hold, titled SafetyHold, which takes no other field), so the commit's OpenHolds.holds takes each hold cut to those three, unchanged (actions/src/commit/types.ts SafetyHold); the rest says where the hold came from. Never the outcome's sealed words, labels or tenses, nor the person's or the turn's text (README item 34). New in v1.3.

blocksBooking.description: safety_holds.blocks_booking (K-09 v1 safetyHold.blocksBooking): the plug-in's stop words matched, so booking stays blocked even after an at-once release (arch 06 line 319; A3-26).

safetyOutcomeId.description: safety_holds.safety_outcome_id: the outcome that set it (one hold per outcome: safety_holds_one_per_outcome).

bookingId.description: safety_holds.booking_id: the booking the held actions are about, or null for a request with no booking yet.

turnId.description: safety_holds.turn_id: the turn whose routine actions wait, or null for page or agent free text (K-34 v1).

version.description: safety_holds.version: a release compares and sets it (K-04 v1 rule 2; K-34 rule 2).

readOpenHolds.request.title: ReadOpenHoldsRequest
readOpenHolds.request.description: What is open on a turn's handle at commit time (the commit's OpenHolds port: actions/src/commit/types.ts; QUESTIONS.md CQ-65 with its DL-119, DL-127, DL-128 and DL-133 addenda: 'the commit path reads them again at commit time, so a hold opened mid-turn binds that commit too'; closes K-05 v1.2 open gap 26). Scope: the request's business, the call's own (arch 10 line 546; K-04 v1 rule 4; K-34 v1 rule 4): with a business it runs as the Tool API's role, rosie_app, inside the call's transaction under that business's scope, since both tables it reads are business-scoped and rosie_app holds SELECT on them (migration 0016); with businessId null (before there is a business) it runs on the runtime side and reads only rows with no business, as readTurnState does (v1.2 item 26, default 25). Reads: the primary, uncached. Repeat: safe, a read (the commit runs it again on a repeated turn: actions/src/commit/types.ts CommitPorts). Time budget: inside 'Gate and commit ≤ 300 ms' (arch 04 line 223). New in v1.3.

handleId.description: The turn's handle (K-05 v1 turn.handleId; K-34 safety_holds.handle_id).

businessId.description: The business the call runs under (the Tool API call's caller.businessId), or null before there is one. Always stated, so the read never runs with no scope by omission (STATE note 22; CQ-70).

eventIds.description: The texts (K-06 v1 event ids) whose safety row the read checks: each of the turn's texts whose recordSafetyOutcome is not among this commit's core actions (an outcome that rides in this commit is written by it, so it is not unread at commit time), and each id the runtime carries as unread (T-1088's CommitContext; DL-127, DL-133: 'any unread id holds, whether or not it is one of the turn's own texts'). Empty when every text's outcome rides in this commit.

readOpenHolds.response.title: ReadOpenHoldsResponse
readOpenHolds.response.description: The commit's OpenHolds as one read of the primary saw it (one read-only transaction, one moment): holds, every open hold on the handle at this business (released_at null), in held_at order, a tie to the lower id (compared, never parsed: CQ-09); unreadEventIds, each of the request's eventIds that no safety_outcomes row the scope shows names (K-34 safety_outcomes_event_key), in the request's order, which holds every part but a protective one (CQ-65's DL-127 addendum; actions/src/commit/hold.ts isHeld). Both lists present, empty when there is none. New in v1.3.

readAt.description: The database's now() at the read.

holds.description: The open holds on the handle at this business (with no business: those with none), held_at order, a tie to the lower id. A released hold is not open and is not listed (README default 45).

unreadEventIds.description: Of the request's eventIds, each with no safety row the scope shows, in the request's order (OpenHolds.unreadEventIds). An outcome row of another business, or one with no business under a business scope, is not seen, so its text counts as unread: the read fails closed (README default 44).

readOpenHolds.errors.title: ReadOpenHoldsErrors
readOpenHolds.errors.description: notFound: the business does not exist, or its own scope does not show it (table businesses), so no answer of 'nothing open' is ever given under a business that is not there; transient. The commit fails closed on either (actions/src/commit/commit.ts: the port's answer is read before any limit runs). New in v1.3.

rowLine.title: RowLine
rowLine.description: Which of Rosie's lines an outbox row carries to its reader: the step (K-01 v1 stepId) and the line's index among that step's lines from Rosie to that reader, in the step's say order, 0 for the first (ComposeRow.step and line; QUESTIONS.md CQ-151 (a) and its default 2). K-04 v1's outbox_rows holds neither (CQ-151 a), so v1.3 says where each comes from in from: openQuestion, the step of the open question the row asks (outbox_rows.open_question_id, open_questions.step: 'The step that asks', K-04 v1), at index 0 (CQ-151 (a)'s default 2). A later minor version adds the row's own stored step and line once K-04 holds them (README open gap 29). New in v1.3.

index.description: The line's index among the step's lines from Rosie to this reader, 0 for the first.

from.description: Where step and index were read from: openQuestion (the row's open question's step; the index is CQ-151 (a)'s default 0).

answeredText.title: AnsweredText
answeredText.description: One text an outbox row answers: a text of the turn that committed the row (K-04 v1 turns.event_ids, in order), by its K-06 v1 event id, with the safety read's plain result for it (K-34 v1 safety_outcomes by event_id: outcomes, what holds after code's rules, and each label's tense), which sets the row's tone (ComposeInput situation: 'a safety outcome other than No' is gentle, arch 07 line 357) and the safety ask a tense unknown adds (arch 06 line 329). Never the text's words, which stay sealed (README item 35: the runtime caller hands them in), and never the outcome's sealed words. outcomes and tenses are null when the scope shows no safety row for the text (its outcome rides in no commit yet, or another business's), and for a clock turn's one event id, which is its clock row's id and names no text (K-05 v1 default 9). New in v1.3.

eventId.description: The text's K-06 v1 event id (turns.event_ids).

outcomes.description: safety_outcomes.outcomes (K-02 v1 safetyResult.outcomes), or null with no row the scope shows.

tenses.description: safety_outcomes.tenses (K-02 v1 safetyLabel.tense, one per label, in the labels' order), or null with no row the scope shows.

rowRecipient.title: RowRecipient
rowRecipient.description: The reader an outbox row goes to, as compose input and finalize read it (K-03 v1 composeInput audience; ComposeRow.role, name, language, allowedFormats; FinalizeRow.reader): its handle's kind (K-04 v1 handles.kind), its person (outbox_rows.recipient_person_id) with the name and language K-04 stores for them (persons.name, persons.language), the person's live roles at the row's business (person_roles with ended_at null), from which the caller takes the one the message is for (identity and access, T-308; S13-31) and limit 7's reader (readerOf), and the phone's flags what this phone allows is built from (C-128; arch 07 line 365). Never the handle's address (the number or the email address): compose input and finalize never need it, and it is never logged or traced (K-08). New in v1.3.

personId.description: outbox_rows.recipient_person_id, or null when not known.

name.description: persons.name as stored ('as they gave it or as a business saved it'), or null until known or with no person. How Rosie addresses the reader from it (K-03 audience.name) is the caller's (README open gap 34).

storedLanguage.description: persons.language: the language Rosie stored for the person (a BCP 47 tag), or null: the business's. The message's language is the text's, else this, else the business's (arch 06; K-03 v1 language): the caller's.

roles.description: The person's live roles at the row's business (person_roles, ended_at null), in role id order; empty for a row with no business or no person.

phone.description: The recipient handle's phone flags (K-04 v1 phones by handle_id: phones_handle_key), or null for an email handle or a number with no phone row yet: stopped, chat open, the service Linq reports, the first poll vote (arch 07 line 379: until then a poll's options also go in the words) and the row's version. Never the number.

chatWay.description: phones.chat_way: imessage, rcs or sms, or null before the first text (Q-33).

businessHeadRead.title: BusinessHeadRead
businessHeadRead.description: A business head row as the slot source reads it (K-04 v1 businesses; CQ-03): the name (biz.name, B01), the display name texts show under the sensitive switch (B02; RULES 4.6), the time zone the reader's day and a deadline are read in when no visit gives one (CQ-05's default; SlotSource.zones.business) and the row's version. New in v1.3.

rowQuestion.title: RowQuestion
rowQuestion.description: The open question an outbox row asks (K-04 v1 open_questions by outbox_rows.open_question_id) with its clock row (clock_rows of kind question for it, which the commit makes once per question and which arms at the first delivery receipt: arch 02 line 127; K-05 v1 items 1 and 5), each at its version: the options as sent (ComposeRow.options), the step that asks (rowLine), the Clock line, and what finalize's passed-on path withdraws with the clock (FinalizeRow.question: QuestionClock; RULES 5.2), whose due time fills ask.by once armed (SlotFacts.askBy). New in v1.3.

options.description: open_questions.options: the options as sent, in order, each label word for word (K-03 option).

clock.description: open_questions.clock: the step's Clock line as it applies, or null (step 9's default).

clockRow.description: The question's clock row (kind question), or null when it has none: its state, due time and zone (null until it arms) and version.

questionAsSent.title: QuestionAsSent
questionAsSent.description: A question still open with the reader, with its words as sent (arch 07 line 389; ComposeRow.openQuestions, K-03 v1 openQuestion {id, text}): a live open question (status waiting or open) sent to the row's recipient handle at the row's business, other than the row's own, that has gone (a part of a row that asks it and goes to that handle is sent or delivered: v1.2 item 26, default 41), with the text of the words send in that row's stored final parts (K-03 finalParts sends, kind words), the newest such row's. The opt-out line in those words is taken out by compose input, never here (DL-245). New in v1.3.

text.description: The words as sent: the words send's text of the newest row that asks it of this handle and has gone.

fixedLineRowError.title: FixedLineRowError
fixedLineRowError.description: The row is a fixed-line row, which is never composed nor finalized (STATE note 17; K-09 v1 open gap 16; ComposeRow and FinalizeRow fixedLineId): a row of send class safety, the checked safety line written word for word (arch 07 line 347: 'Safety lines stay fixed text'; arch 02 line 111; K-09 v1 recordSafetyOutcome safetyLine). Nothing else is returned, so no composer input is ever built from it; compose input and finalize refuse the row as their handlers refuse a fixedLineId (README item 35). New in v1.3.

readOutboxRow.request.title: ReadOutboxRowRequest
readOutboxRow.request.description: An outbox row as compose input and finalize read it (ComposeInputPorts.readRow: actions/src/compose-input/types.ts; FinalizePorts.readRow: actions/src/finalize/rewrite/types.ts; K-09 v1 composeInput.request 'the row and today's record', finalizeMessage.request 'the row, its slots' values and the reader's audience'; arch 07 line 397). Scope: the request's business, the call's own. With a business it runs as rosie_job inside the call's transaction with rosie.business_id set to it and confirmed by requireBusinessScope() before the first read (STATE note 22; T-1094's note N2), since it also reads tables only the runtime side holds (turns, persons, handles, phones, outbox_parts: migration 0012), as readTurnState does (v1.2 item 26), and every read of a business-scoped table also names the business; with businessId null it runs on the runtime side and reads only a row with no business (Rosie's own lines before there is one). Reads: the primary, uncached. Repeat: safe, a read. Time budget: none in the sources (inside the compose and finalize hops). New in v1.3.

outboxRowId.description: The row (K-09 v1 composeInput.request and finalizeMessage.request outboxRowId).

businessId.description: The business the call runs under (caller.businessId), or null before there is one. Always stated (STATE note 22; CQ-70).

readOutboxRow.response.title: ReadOutboxRowResponse
readOutboxRow.response.description: The row as one read of the primary saw it (one read-only transaction, one moment): row, what K-04 v1 outbox_rows holds that compose input and finalize read; line, its step and line (rowLine; null for a row that asks no question: README open gap 29); recipient, its reader (rowRecipient); answers, the texts it answers by event id with their safety results, never their words; slotSource, the record its slots are filled from that K-04 v1 holds (the business head, the booking head, the question it asks); openQuestions, the other questions still open with the reader with their words as sent. What the caller adds, field by field, is in README item 35's table: the inbound words (handed in by the runtime caller), the bundle's master line, links and checks, and code's rules. Every list is present, empty when there is none. Never a sealed value, the inbound words, the recipient's address, a key or a wrapping key's name (rule 7). New in v1.3.

readAt.description: The database's now() at the read.

row.description: K-04 v1 outbox_rows as compose input and finalize read it.

turnId.description: outbox_rows.turn_id: the turn that committed it (K-03 composeInput turn).

bundleId.description: outbox_rows.bundle_hash and bundle_build: the bundle it was committed under, whose step line, links and checks are read (arch 10 line 548; ComposeRow.bundleId).

version.description: outbox_rows.version: finalize's expectVersion must be it (FinalizeRow.version; limit 4 at writePlan).

sendClass.description: outbox_rows.send_class: routine, quick_reply or visit_now; a safety row answers fixedLineRow instead (README item 35).

copyOfRowId.description: outbox_rows.copy_of_row_id: for an email copy, the text row whose plan it takes, else null (ComposeRow.copyOfRowId).

hasPlan.description: Whether outbox_rows.plan is not null (ComposeRow.hasPlan: a planned row is never composed again, arch 11 line 576). The plan itself is not returned.

finalParts.description: outbox_rows.final_parts (K-03 v1 finalParts), or null while it holds none (FinalizeRow.finalParts).

line.description: The step and line the row carries to its reader (rowLine), or null when K-04 v1 cannot say: a row that asks no question (README open gap 29). Compose input and finalize refuse a row whose line is null (fail closed), never guess one.

answers.description: The texts the row answers: the turn that committed it (turns by outbox_rows.turn_id), the handle its texts came from (turns.handle_id), so the words go to the composer only in a reply to their own sender (arch 07 line 397; ComposeRow.inbound.fromHandleId), and its texts in turn order (answeredText). Their words are handed in by the runtime caller by event id (README item 35, default 47).

handleId.description: turns.handle_id: the handle the turn's texts came from.

texts.description: turns.event_ids in order, each with its safety result.

slotSource.description: The record the row's slots are filled from, as far as K-04 v1 holds it (SlotSource: actions/src/finalize/slots/types.ts; T-310): the business head (null for a row with no business), the booking head with its flags (null for a row about no booking; v1.2 bookingHead) and the question the row asks with its clock row (null when it asks none). A slot whose home is not here is left out, so the slots that read it stay unfilled (SlotFacts: 'A fact left out leaves the slots that read it unfilled'), and the Values check refuses a message that needs it (arch 07 line 409). The sensitive switch is not read here (README open gap 30): a row about a booking is filled as if it were on, the stricter (RULES 4.6).

openQuestions.description: The questions still open with the reader, other than the row's own, each with its words as sent (questionAsSent), in id order (compared, never parsed: CQ-09).

readOutboxRow.errors.title: ReadOutboxRowErrors
readOutboxRow.errors.description: notFound: no such row, or the scope hides it (another business's row, or a row with a business read with businessId null: table outbox_rows), as K-09 v1's composeInput and finalizeMessage answer it; fixedLineRow: a safety row, never composed nor finalized; transient. Nothing is returned with any of them. New in v1.3.

readFixedLineFacts.request.title: ReadFixedLineFactsRequest
readFixedLineFacts.request.description: What the fixed-line inserter needs to know about a row's handle and business (FixedLinePorts.readFixedLines: actions/src/finalize/fixed-lines/types.ts; arch 07 line 361: 'on Rosie's first text to a handle about one business (DD), the opener ... and the privacy-notice link; and on a number's texts until one is delivered, the STOP, HELP and rates line'). The call takes only the row: its recipient handle and business are read from the row itself, never handed in, so no caller can ask about another handle. Scope: the request's business, the call's own. With a business it runs as rosie_job inside the finalize call's transaction with rosie.business_id set to it and confirmed by requireBusinessScope() before the first read (STATE note 22), since the phone row is a runtime-only table (migration 0012; T-220's sendState reads it on the runtime side only), and every read of a business-scoped table also names the business; with businessId null it runs on the runtime side and reads only a row with no business. Reads: the primary, uncached. Repeat: safe, a read. Time budget: none in the sources (inside the finalize hop). New in v1.3.

outboxRowId.description: The row the final parts are for (FinalizeRow.outboxRowId).

businessId.description: The business the call runs under (caller.businessId), or null before there is one. Always stated (STATE note 22; CQ-70).

readFixedLineFacts.response.title: ReadFixedLineFactsResponse
readFixedLineFacts.response.description: FixedLineFacts' two database facts for the row (README item 36), from one read of the primary: textedAboutBusiness and optOutLineDeliveredAt under the port's own names, with the opener mark that decides the first (openerRowId). The row's other fixed lines (FixedLineFacts.lines) are not database facts here (README open gap 36). Never the phone's number or the handle's address. New in v1.3.

recipientHandleId.description: outbox_rows.recipient_handle_id: the handle both facts are about.

readAt.description: The database's now() at the read.

textedAboutBusiness.description: Whether Rosie has texted this handle about the row's business before (FixedLineFacts.textedAboutBusiness): true when the opener mark for the handle and the business (K-04 v1 openers_sent, 'Whether Rosie's opener for a business has gone to a handle') names another row; false when there is none, or it names this row, which then is the first text and carries the opener again. With no business, true when an earlier row to the handle with no business (a lower commit_seq) carries the opener in its stored final parts (fixedLines holds K-01's opener), since openers_sent holds no row with no business (README item 36, default 50).

openerRowId.description: The row the opener went on: openers_sent.outbox_row_id for the handle and the business, or with no business the earliest earlier row that carries it; null when there is none.

optOutLineDeliveredAt.description: phones.optout_line_delivered_at of the recipient handle's phone (K-04 v1 phones by handle_id: phones_handle_key; FixedLineFacts.optOutLineDeliveredAt): when the STOP, HELP and rates line was first delivered to the number, or null while none of its texts that carried it was delivered, and for an email handle or a number with no phone row (RULES 4.3; Q-30).

readFixedLineFacts.errors.title: ReadFixedLineFactsErrors
readFixedLineFacts.errors.description: notFound: no such row, or the scope hides it (table outbox_rows); transient. The finalize call answers either as its own (K-09 v1 finalizeMessage.errors) and writes nothing. New in v1.3.
